name: BTC one-minute EMA(9)/EMA(21) cross state
description: A causal reading over the ready `btc.external.spot_reference@1.0.0` blended reference price, sampled once per second on the lane decision clock. Ema_9 and ema_21 are exponential moving averages of the one-minute bar closes with smoothing factor alpha equal to two divided by (period plus one) — 0.2 and approximately 0.09090909 respectively. Each is seeded with the arithmetic mean of its first `period` closes and advanced as previous value plus alpha times (current close minus previous value). spread_bps is (ema_9 minus ema_21) divided by ema_21, times ten thousand. state is bullish when spread_bps is positive, bearish when it is negative, and flat when it is exactly zero. crossed_present is true once a sign change of spread_bps has been observed since continuity started, and crossed_at is the bar close at which that change was observed; while crossed_present is false, crossed_at repeats window_close and carries no cross information. The nine- and twenty-one-bar lengths are initial research defaults that require empirical calibration; the exponential-moving-average recursion is not a heuristic threshold. One-minute bars are closed on the lane decision clock at minute boundaries from the one-second sample series: open is the first sample of the minute, high and low its extrema, close its last sample. A bar that is missing any one-second sample is invalid; the missing sample breaks continuity, every retained bar and every smoothed state derived from them is discarded, and the bar warm-up restarts from the next whole bar. Nothing is bridged across a gap. Ready once twenty-one contiguous one-minute bars have closed (the longer average's seed). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Every reading is causal: it reads only samples at or before the decision it is published on. Adopted in the C3a TA pack (ruling E51, 2026-09-04): the seven technical-analysis identities are published on every price venue we carry, computed from the venue's own one-second sample ring by the shared `crates/btc-signals/src/ta.rs` helper, so every scope runs byte-identical arithmetic and only the sample series differs.
